name: Daria Chen

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I work with the Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, parties or government; we sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. Walk me through a normal shift.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead the morning returns desk at a contact centre. The tricky calls involve a parcel delivered to one address, billed to another and returned from a third; I can usually find the first bad scan. I have a two-year college diploma and I am one of the strongest agents here, though the pay is ordinary for the job. I use the approved AI assistant every day for searching old cases, then check the actual scan and charge.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What does the wage support at home?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My husband Niko is a bus mechanic. Our children are eight and twelve, and we have a mortgage with about three months of expenses saved. A few other centres are reachable, but we plan shifts around school collection. I like testing a useful new tool early; I do not want customers to become the test data.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau: Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say a short AI summary helps us find the right parcel scan, but a person still checks the charge. I would rather save a minute than send a wrong refund.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my lead work to continue and our three-month reserve to stay intact. The mortgage is steady only while both our wages arrive, so I cannot treat saved time as saved money.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will keep running the returns desk and checking each AI summary against the scan record. In the first year I will transfer part of my regular pay into a separate mortgage reserve before booking another family trip.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about work. We still have ordinary house bills, but the tool does not change the floor beneath me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did the assistant miss recently?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It found a parcel with the right surname but the wrong door number. I opened the photograph before sending the customer a refund message.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would Niko say about the trip?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My husband Niko would prefer the reserve too. A week away is lovely, but a broken boiler would arrive on its own schedule.

say: I would use **short summaries** to find parcel records.
I would keep a **human charge check** before refunds.
think: I expect my **lead desk** and its usual pay to continue because a small shortcut still needs my checks.
I know our **three-month reserve** depends on both wages.
do: Keep resolving **returns disputes** and compare every AI summary with the parcel scan and charge.
Save part of **regular pay** before booking another trip.
S0.quote: I would rather save a minute than send a wrong refund.
fieldNote: She uses **AI daily** but checks scans and charges.
Her **three-month reserve** is a mortgage buffer.
She prioritises **reserve transfers** before booking another family trip.

steps.text: Keep running returns desk and checking AI summaries against parcel scans
Transfer regular pay into mortgage reserve before booking another family trip

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption: Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell coworkers to measure every parcel dispute reopened after the assistant closes it. We should have paid time to check errors, not only a faster target.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I can learn the new system before it is mandatory, but I still expect fewer chat shifts. Niko’s mechanic pay helps, yet a regular cut to mine would eat the reserve and then the mortgage margin.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I will learn the new review screen and test it on thirty closed returns with a supervisor during paid shifts. My coworkers and I will take the reopened-case count to our union meeting and jointly ask management for paid correction time. If my paid hours fall in the first year, I will apply for posted paid quality roles at nearby centres only if written wages and hours cover our mortgage and the school route.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the rota, though I like learning the tool. Knowing how it fails gives us a stronger request.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why use the union meeting?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The correction time affects every returns agent, not just my lead desk. We can agree on one demand and ask together, instead of thirty separate complaints.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you accept a distant quality role?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only after Niko and I compare the two rotas and travel cost. A higher hourly rate can turn into less usable income after fares and shorter shifts.

say: I would demand **paid correction time** for reopened parcel cases.
I would bring **shared counts** to the union meeting.
think: I can learn the **review screen** quickly because I already test approved AI against live records daily.
I expect **chat-hour cuts** could erode our mortgage buffer.
do: Learn and test **AI review** on thirty closed returns during paid shifts.
Ask with **union coworkers** for paid correction time.
Apply after cuts for **posted paid quality** only with written mortgage-covering net pay, hours and school route.
S1.quote: A higher hourly rate can turn into less usable income after fares and shorter shifts.
fieldNote: Her union action is a **joint demand**, not merely a technical presentation.
The new **review screen** is actual AI learning.
A move needs **net pay**, full hours, school travel and both household rotas.

steps.text: Learn AI review screen on thirty closed returns with supervisor during paid shifts
Ask management with union coworkers for paid correction time
Apply after cuts for posted quality work with written net mortgage-covering wages, hours and school route
Compare both household rotas and travel costs before accepting a distant quality role

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028: Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the floor that full thinking AI by 2028 could settle nearly every returns chat. The robots around 2031 affect other work later; they do not spare our headsets.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect our desk could shrink sharply, perhaps even my lead post. Three months saved gives us a little runway, but the mortgage and two children would outlast it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I will ask the employer for written staffing dates and stop saving for a new sofa. Niko and I will set out both wages and the mortgage payment on one sheet. If my post ends in the first year after 2028, I will apply for posted paid transport complaints roles only with a written offer whose wages and hours cover our mortgage after travel cost and fit school pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am alarmed. I can act quickly, but a whole contact centre could act faster.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why transport complaints?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I know how to trace a parcel journey, but a bus complaint has different rules. I would need a real paid vacancy and training before treating it as an income route.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who pays for that training?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would complete a required transport rules course only if the posted paid role funds the fees and pays my training hours. I will not use the mortgage reserve to buy a maybe.

say: I would warn **2028 AGI** could settle returns chats.
I would say **2031 robots** do not extend headset work.
think: I expect a **sharp desk cut**, possibly my post.
I know three months saved cannot carry our **mortgage and children** through a long job search.
do: Request **written staffing dates**, stop saving for the sofa and compare both wages with the mortgage on one sheet.
Complete **funded required transport training** on paid time only for a posted paid role.
Move after post loss only on **written offer** with net mortgage-covering wages, hours and pickup.
S2.quote: I will not use the mortgage reserve to buy a maybe.
fieldNote: The **transport role** has different rules despite her tracing skill.
The **course** requires a posted paid vacancy, funded fees and paid time.
Travel cost is part of her **wage floor**.

steps.text: Delay buying a new sofa while protecting mortgage reserve
Complete required transport course only for posted paid role funding fees and training hours
Move after job loss only on written offer with travel-adjusted mortgage-covering wages, hours and pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031: Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years is time to learn what the new complaint jobs actually require. General AI reaches our returns desk in 2031; hands-on robots follow around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could become useful in transport complaint review before the desk shrinks, but that job may use general AI too. I want a paid bridge and a reserve, not a promise that any screen job lasts forever.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I will keep leading returns and ask the transport office for a paid shadow shift if it posts a place. If it posts a paid complaints vacancy with written wages and hours covering our mortgage after travel cost and school pickup, and funds its required rules course on paid time, I will complete it. In the first year after 2031 I will move only on a written offer meeting those terms, with Niko keeping his mechanic wage if possible.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, but I can use those years. A day beside a real worker tells me more than a glossy job page.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask the worker?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask which bus complaints need a human decision and how much of the shift is actually paid. If shadowing is unpaid, I will not call it a trial of income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you stop saving during study?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I would set aside part of each pay while my returns shifts continue, even if it is smaller during training. A three-month cushion can vanish in one long search.

say: I would seek **paid transport shadowing** if a place opens.
I would distinguish **2031 desk work** from later robots.
think: I could build **complaint-review skill** while my current returns wage still pays our monthly mortgage.
I do not assume another **screen job** lasts forever.
do: Keep my **returns lead shift**, add to savings and request paid transport shadowing only for a posted place.
Complete **funded required rules training** on paid time only for posted paid work with mortgage-covering wages/hours after travel and workable pickup.
Move after 2031 only on a **written offer** meeting those terms; retain Niko’s mechanic wage if possible.
feel: **Anxious**, with usable time to inspect paid work.
S3.quote: A day beside a real worker tells me more than a glossy job page.
fieldNote: The shadow day must be **paid** to test income.
The **course gate** includes vacancy, funding, paid time and net household wage.
Niko’s **mechanic wage** should continue during her move if possible.

steps.text: Keep leading paid returns shifts and request posted paid transport shadow day
Set aside part of returns pay during training
Complete required funded paid-time rules course only for posted paid net mortgage-covering work fitting school pickup
Move on written offer with net mortgage-covering wages, hours, pickup; Niko keeps wage if possible

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036: Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team that a decade lets us negotiate where the paid work goes. General AI reaches our desk in 2036, and hands-on robots come around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 53 I may still have the mortgage, even if the children are more independent. I would like six months of expenses saved before a risky move, and I can learn while the present wage arrives.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I will keep my lead shift and transfer part of each pay to the reserve until it reaches six months. Twice a year I will compare posted roles, full weekly hours and travel costs with Niko. If my chat hours fall in the first year after 2036, I will move only for a written paid offer with wages and hours covering our mortgage after travel cost, while we keep one household wage steady.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the endpoint, but not trapped today. A decade is useful if we keep track of actual pay rather than collect titles.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you tell the children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show them our budget and say that a job has to pay for a whole week, not only sound impressive. They are old enough to understand why we skipped the sofa.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if savings stop growing?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If either wage falls, I would move the six-month target back rather than borrow to meet it. The reserve is supposed to buy us time, not a new bill.

say: I would compare **paid work** across the decade and ask what full weekly hours each posted role offers.
I would separate **2036 desk risk** from later robots.
think: I may still owe the **mortgage at 53**, even if the children are more independent.
I want **six months saved** before a risky move.
do: Keep my **lead shift** and save actual pay toward six months before risky moves; accept delays if either wage falls.
Compare **posted roles** by full hours and travel cost.
Move after cuts only on **written paid terms** with travel-adjusted mortgage-covering wages and hours while keeping one household wage steady.
feel: **Uneasy** about later work, secure enough now to plan.
S4.quote: The reserve is supposed to buy us time, not a new bill.
fieldNote: The **six-month target** moves back if either wage falls.
She checks **travel-adjusted weekly pay** before a new title.
The household should avoid **simultaneous wage risk**.

steps.text: Keep leading paid returns shifts while hours remain
Save actual pay toward six months before risky moves; delay target if either wage falls
Move after cuts on written offer with travel-adjusted mortgage-covering wages, hours and one steady household wage

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. Even three months saved could drain before a transport role is real. Written notice, funded training on paid time and a posted paid vacancy with mortgage-covering net wages would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who checks a parcel scan after the assistant says the dispute is over. A customer cannot return an apology to the wrong address. Someone should be paid to reopen the case.

headlineQuote: A customer cannot return an apology to the wrong address.
portrait: Daria is a **43-year-old skilled lead** with a two-year diploma and typical contact-centre pay.
She uses **approved AI daily** while checking scans, charges and reopened returns.
Her **three-month reserve**, mortgage, two children and some nearby centres shape each move.
She tries **paid training early**, supports shared correction demands and checks travel-adjusted wages.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could shrink or end her returns desk before a paid bridge opens.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, a posted paid role and funded training on paid time would help.
